subject: Fat-tail surge proofing for private VPC fleet — capacity & network thresholds
messages:
From: Acme Ops <ops@acme.co>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fat-tail surge profile for private fleet — load sketches and asks

Hi Priya / team,

Quick context: we're planning a private VPC deployment of Redwood for our customer-facing inference (logistics ETA, multi-step planning). Attached is a sampled workload profile from September (hourly traces and a few 15-min hammer windows). We have a couple of immediate asks: 

- Can you propose sustained throughput targets per GPU and recommended burst headroom to survive a fat-tail event (20x baseline for 5-10 minutes)?
- Any network/egress hard limits we should plan for (we have a 40Gbps egress cap in our datacenter rack)?
- Thermal or power concerns if we hold 20x for >10m across a rack?

We'd like a one-page operational runway (numbers + quick mitigation steps) to circulate to platform ops and procurement by EOD Thursday.

Attachments: acme_workload_profile.csv (sampled traces, 9MB)

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Ops Lead, Acme Logistics

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Ops <ops@acme.co>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-11T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fat-tail surge profile for private fleet — load sketches and asks

Hi Amit — thanks for the traces, good signal. High level answers and an operational runway below. I attached a short sim workbook with the run numbers (runway_simulation_v3.xlsx).

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline target: provision for sustained 1.2x of median QPS for steady-state (keeps cost predictable).
- Burst headroom: reserve a burst pool equivalent to 8–10x median per-rack capacity to absorb 5–10m spikes. For your 20x fat-tail we recommend a two-tier response: immediate admission control + temporary burst slab.
- Admission control: set admission drop to start at 12x sustained and progressive shedding by priority down to 20% of background for best-effort flows.
- Network cap planning: with 40Gbps egress limit, cap token throughput per GPU to avoid queue blowouts — aim for per-GPU egress <= 12 Gbps during bursts (assumes batch packing and kv-cache reuse).
- Thermal/power: avoid holding 20x across >6 GPUs per rack for >8 minutes without active thermal ramp-down; include staggered warm-pool drains.

Technical rationale (brief):
- We simulated your traces across our 4 common model families (base/quant/seq-long/multitoken). The dominant cost at 20x is network egress + KV cache miss amplification; batching helps but increases per-token latency at tail.
- A burst slab (hot spare GPUs in an isolated slab) lets you absorb spikes without cascading queue growth; eviction policy is LRU prefix-aware to preserve active sessions.

Recommended runway (numbers):
- Median QPS observed: 12k QPS cluster-wide -> baseline provision: 14.4k QPS (1.2x).
- Provision per GPU (A100 / v3-like perf): ~800 sustained QPS -> baseline GPUs: 18
- Burst slab: +12 GPUs reserved (elastic slab) to handle 8–10x short spikes (sustained <10m)
- Admission control thresholds: 12x start shed, 16x progressive shed, >20x emergency reject
- Network headroom: reserve 30% of rack egress for control plane + cache sync during bursts -> leaves ~28Gbps for token egress on a 40Gbps link.

Operational asks for Acme ops:
1) Run an isolated 2-hour stress window on your staging rack that emulates the 20x 10-minute event (we can provide the load generator).
2) Share thermal/power headroom per rack (sustained TDP margin) so we can refine the >8min guidance.
3) Accept a canary: we'll push a canary that activates the burst slab with auto-evict and a tighter admission curve to validate rollback behavior.

I'll leave numbers in the workbook; happy to walk through on a quick call.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runway_simulation_v3.xlsx]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Oct 11, 2027 at 11:32 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Executive summary (short):
> - Baseline target: provision for sustained 1.2x of median QPS for steady-state...

Thanks Priya — a couple of ops-minded clarifications and a small alternative we should include in the runway doc: 

1) Thermal/EGRESS interplay: if a rack hits sustained high egress and high PCIe throughput, internal PDU sag can appear before thermal alarms. Ops should instrument PDU current at 1s resolution during stress windows. If PDU headroom <15% during 20x events we recommend preemptive shed.

2) Batch packing + prefix cache: to keep effective egress under 12Gbps/GPU during a spike, we should plan RPC-level batching (pack up to 3 concurrent small requests) and warm the prefix cache per customer shard during pre-warm windows. This reduces both GPU cycles and egress amplification.

3) Multiplex guardrail: define max-tenancy-per-GPU (we recommend 6 concurrent sessions for low-latency SLA tiers) — anything above should be routed to best-effort pools with higher admission thresholds.

4) Canary plan (concrete):
- Phase A: staging stress test (ops runs generator) — observe PDU/thermal for 2h.
- Phase B: canary on 10% production traffic into burst slab for 48h, with auto rollback on 3x SLO breaches.

I've embedded a small diagram of network thresholds in the shared drive and attached a quick PNG here for their infra team.

Jonas
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network_thresholds_diagram.png]

Short note from the commercial side: 

- If Acme plans to keep a dedicated burst slab (12 GPUs reserved) we'll need to align on a Reserved Burst SKU vs. pure on-demand. That SKU affects monthly minimums and the SLA for burst availability.
- For the canary window: we can include a temporary credit line if the 48h canary trips an SLO — helps de-risk testing for procurement.

Priya/Jonas — can you confirm: with the recommended 18 baseline + 12 burst GPUs, what's the expected 99.9th percentile latency delta during a 10m 20x spike (ballpark)? We need that number to model the SLA exception in the quote.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is exactly the level we needed. A couple of quick commits from Acme: 

1) We will schedule the staging stress test for Thursday 10/14 22:00–00:00 PT and will provide PDU + thermal logs.
2) We accept the 10% canary plan for Phase B but request a rollback threshold at 2x SLO breaches (we have tighter uptime needs).
3) On reserved SKU: procurement is open to a small reserved burst commitment if Redwood can provide a 45% discount on burst-hours over 6 months (we'll draft an initial term sheet).

We'll upload logs to the shared drive and ping HBSP-48271 when ready. Please confirm the canary activation checklist (we want a go/no-go gate one hour before ramp).
